title: Amhara Spiced Lamb Stew
community: Amhara people — the highland Christian majority
author: Mama Tigist

heritage.origin: Amhara region — the political and cultural heartland of highland Ethiopia
heritage.history: The Amhara are the largest ethnic group in Ethiopia's highland regions and the source of much of what the world considers 'Ethiopian cuisine' — the injera, the berbere wat tradition, and the coffee ceremony all have deep Amhara roots. Amhara lamb wat is the celebration dish of the Ethiopian highlands — made for Ethiopian Orthodox holidays, family gatherings, and the breaking of major fasts. The lamb is cooked using the dry-caramelised onion technique that Amhara cooks have perfected over centuries, with more berbere than the standard recipe and the addition of cardamom and rue.

desc: Amhara Lamb Wat — bone-in highland lamb simmered for 90 minutes in a deeply spiced berbere sauce built on dry-caramelised onions and kibbeh. The celebration wat of the Amhara highlands — more berbere, more kibbeh, and the addition of korerima (Ethiopian black cardamom).
longDesc: Amhara Beg Wat is the prestige lamb dish of highland Ethiopia — richer than standard Key Wat, with the bone-in lamb releasing collagen into the sauce and the korerima adding a smoky camphor note that defines authentic Amhara cooking.
steps: Add kibbeh. Add berbere. Fry 4 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, tomato paste, korerima, and rue.
Add water. Simmer covered 80—90 minutes until lamb is very tender.
chefTips: Korerima (Ethiopian black cardamom) is the Amhara signature — irreplaceable.
Bone-in lamb releases collagen — the sauce should be thick and glossy.
cookingScience: See ETH021 for lamb wat science.
sustainabilityTips: Ethiopian highland lamb — particularly flavourful from highland grasses.
culturalNote: Amhara lamb wat is eaten at the Meskel celebration, at Fasika (Easter), and at every significant family gathering in the Amhara highlands. The quality of the wat served at a celebration tells the guests everything they need to know about the host's respect for them.
